supported_scope: Persistent project instructions stored as rules in .agents/rules/ and managed via CLI
unestablished_scope: Automatic precedence resolution details beyond directory specificity
Instruction discovery mechanisms beyond filesystem rules
Supported instruction formats beyond YAML frontmatter and action(target) rules
required_setup: Create and maintain rules files in .agents/rules/ with YAML frontmatter; optionally share rules via .agents/rules.json; manage permissions and agent instructions via CLI commands and file system
constraints: Rules must follow YAML frontmatter schema with trigger keys (always_on, model_decision, glob, manual)
Rules are cumulative and combined across global, workspace, and directory scopes
More specific directory rules take precedence over global or workspace rules
Permissions rules follow action(target) format and require explicit allow/deny/ask settings
CLI permissions require interactive management or manual config file editing

evidence.quote: Rules are persistent instructions, coding standards, and architectural constraints that shape how Antigravity behaves in your codebase.
evidence.claim: Persistent instructions are supported as rules shaping agent behavior

evidence.quote: Antigravity discovers rules across multiple scopes, listed below in order of precedence (highest to lowest). Rules are cumulative rather than replacement-based: Antigravity combines all discovered rules across global, workspace, and directory scopes into the prompt.
evidence.claim: Rules are discovered from multiple scopes and combined cumulatively with precedence

evidence.section: Rules > YAML frontmatter and activation modes > Supported frontmatter keys
evidence.quote: Rules in .agents/rules/ support the following YAML frontmatter keys: trigger : model_decision # Required: always_on | model_decision | glob | manual
evidence.claim: Supported instruction formats include YAML frontmatter with trigger keys

evidence.section: CLI best practices > Configure your workspace environment > Write a codebase rule file
evidence.quote: Create a GEMINI.md or AGENTS.md file at your workspace root to outline specific directory standards, styling paradigms, test command parameters, and deprecation warnings. The agent automatically parses these rules on startup and consults them before suggesting changes.
evidence.claim: Instructions persist in workspace root files and are automatically parsed and applied
